title: Gastrodin alleviates mitochondrial energy metabolism dysfunction via activating beta-catenin/c-Myc/MCT2 signaling in Alzheimer's disease models.
authors: Lei, Hui-Ping; Yang, Xue; Hu, Yue-Ting; Wu, Ling-Nan; Wei, Ai-Hong; Yu, Lin; Liu, Ting-Ting; Ji, Xin-Hao; Liu, Ju; Jin, Hai; Zhou, Shao-Yu; Jin, Feng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天麻素通过β-catenin/c-Myc/MCT2信号轴改善AD模型能量代谢，虽含分子对接和ChIP，但核心是药物机制而非TF-DNA互作建模，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Gastrodia elata, also known as Chijian, belongs to the Orchidaceae family of plants. The "Compendium of Materia Medica" records that Gastrodia elata treats "confused speech, excessive fear, and loss of willpower". Gastrodin (GAS) is the main bioactive component of Gastrodia elata. Research has shown that GAS possesses protective effects on multiple animal models of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the exact molecular mechanism of GAS-mediated neuroprotection in AD pathology remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to determine whether GAS exerts neuroprotective effects on AD models through regulating beta-catenin/c-Myc/MCT2 signaling axis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Behavioral and histopathological tests, including Morris water maze test, Nissl staining, and NeuN immunofluorescence staining in 3 x Tg-AD male mice, were used to assess the pharmacological effect of GAS on AD. To investigate the neuroprotective mechanisms of GAS, we established an in vitro AD model using Abeta(25-35)-treated HT22 cells. The expressions of proteins and mRNA related to the beta-catenin/c-Myc signaling axis were determined by western blotting and quantitative PCR. The change in energy metabolism was evaluated by measuring pyruvate, cellular ATP production, and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). The molecular mechanism of GAS-mediated neuroprotection was further explored using pharmacological and genetic interventions targeting beta-catenin and c-Myc. Transcriptional regulation was interrogated through beta-catenin chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) coupled with JASPAR-based motif prediction, while ligand-receptor interactions were characterized by AutoDock-based molecular docking validated through drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS) assay and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). RESULTS: In vivo experimental results revealed that GAS ameliorated cognitive impairment in 3 x Tg-AD mice, attenuated neuronal damage, and markedly inhibited the downregulation of active-beta-catenin, c-Myc, and MCT2 in the hippocampal tissues. In Abeta(25-35)-challenged HT22 cells, the relevant protein levels of beta-catenin/c-Myc signaling axis were reduced, with both mRNA and protein expressions of MCT2 declining, alongside reductions in pyruvate and ATP concentrations. GAS treatment reversed these pathological alterations, while this effect was antagonized by beta-catenin and c-Myc inhibitors. Additionally, lentiviral-mediated beta-catenin overexpression markedly increased MCT2 mRNA and protein expression in HT22 cells. The results of chromatin immunoprecipitation assay coupled with quantitative PCR and JASPAR-based motif prediction revealed that beta-catenin bound to the MCT2 promoter region. Autodock Vina simulation demonstrated that GAS binds to beta-catenin with a binding energy of less than -5 kcal/mol. Both DARTS and CETSA experiments showed that the binding of GAS to beta-catenin protects the beta-catenin protein from degradation. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that GAS plays a protective role in experimental AD models through enhancing MCT2 expression and improving mitochondrial energy metabolism function by activation of the beta-catenin/c-Myc/MCT2 signaling axis.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：天麻（Gastrodia elata），又称赤箭，属于兰科植物。《本草纲目》记载天麻治疗“语多恍惚、多惊失志”。天麻素（GAS）是天麻的主要生物活性成分。研究表明，GAS对多种阿尔茨海默病（AD）动物模型具有保护作用。然而，GAS在AD病理中介导神经保护的确切分子机制仍不清楚。研究目的：本研究旨在确定GAS是否通过调节beta-catenin/c-Myc/MCT2信号轴对AD模型发挥神经保护作用。材料与方法：采用行为学和组织病理学测试，包括Morris水迷宫测试、尼氏染色和NeuN免疫荧光染色，在3 x Tg-AD雄性小鼠中评估GAS对AD的药理作用。为探究GAS的神经保护机制，我们使用Abeta(25-35)处理的HT22细胞建立了体外AD模型。通过western blotting和定量PCR测定与beta-catenin/c-Myc信号轴相关的蛋白质和mRNA表达。通过测量丙酮酸、细胞ATP产生和线粒体膜电位（MMP）评估能量代谢的变化。进一步使用靶向beta-catenin和c-Myc的药理学和遗传学干预手段，探究GAS介导神经保护的分子机制。通过beta-catenin染色质免疫沉淀（ChIP）结合基于JASPAR的基序预测研究转录调控，而配体-受体相互作用通过基于AutoDock的分子对接表征，并经药物亲和力响应靶标稳定性（DARTS）测定和细胞热位移测定（CETSA）验证。结果：体内实验结果显示，GAS改善了3 x Tg-AD小鼠的认知障碍，减轻了神经元损伤，并显著抑制了海马组织中活性beta-catenin、c-Myc和MCT2的下调。在Abeta(25-35)刺激的HT22细胞中，beta-catenin/c-Myc信号轴相关蛋白水平降低，MCT2的mRNA和蛋白表达均下降，同时丙酮酸和ATP浓度减少。GAS处理逆转了这些病理改变，而这一效应被beta-catenin和c-Myc抑制剂拮抗。此外，慢病毒介导的beta-catenin过表达显著增加了HT22细胞中MCT2的mRNA和蛋白表达。染色质免疫沉淀结合定量PCR和基于JASPAR的基序预测结果显示，beta-catenin与MCT2启动子区域结合。AutoDock Vina模拟表明，GAS与beta-catenin的结合能低于-5 kcal/mol。DARTS和CETSA实验均显示，GAS与beta-catenin的结合保护beta-catenin蛋白免于降解。结论：本研究证明，GAS通过激活beta-catenin/c-Myc/MCT2信号轴，增强MCT2表达并改善线粒体能量代谢功能，在实验性AD模型中发挥保护作用。
